# proxmox_node_certificate (Resource)

Installs a custom TLS certificate chain and key for one node through `/nodes/{node}/certificates/custom`, replacing the self-signed certificate. Destroy removes the custom certificate, so the node falls back to its previous one. The private key and chain are sensitive but can be read back from the API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "proxmox_node_certificate" "pve1" {
  node         = "pve-1"
  certificates = file("pve1-chain.pem")
  key          = file("pve1-key.pem")
  force        = true
  restart      = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `certificates` (String, Sensitive) PEM encoded certificate chain, leaf first.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) PEM encoded private key.
- `node` (String) Cluster node. Changes require replacement.

### Optional

- `force` (Boolean) Replace even if the new certificate is invalid (for example self-signed without a matching SAN).
- `restart` (Boolean) Restart pveproxy after installing.

### Read-Only

- `fingerprint` (String) SHA-256 fingerprint of the installed certificate.
- `id` (String) Node name.
- `issuer` (String) Issuer distinguished name.
- `not_after` (String) End of validity.
- `not_before` (String) Start of validity.
- `public_key_bits` (Number) Public key size.
- `public_key_type` (String) Public key algorithm.
- `san` (List of String) Subject alternative names.
- `subject` (String) Subject distinguished name.
